name: Incremental Lighting for In-Scattering
definition: An extension to incremental lighting that approximates light scattering (translucency) by propagating and blurring indirect lighting components from slice to slice, considering only incoming light within a cone in the direction of the light source.
summary: Incremental Lighting for In-Scattering is a screen-space technique that approximates volumetric light scattering by propagating indirect lighting and applying per-channel attenuation to simulate color-changing penetration.
